PullRequest.Title: Add Copilot agent body language features
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Adds Copilot-specific `*.agent.md` body language features on top of #342887.

- Completes the seven case-sensitive Copilot body placeholders:
  - `{{cwd}}`
  - `{{homedir}}`
  - `{{configDir}}`
  - `{{grepToolName}}`
  - `{{globToolName}}`
  - `{{shellToolName}}`
  - `{{shellCommandExamples}}`
- Adds placeholder parsing, hovers, and semantic highlighting.
- Marks unknown Copilot placeholders unused.
- Stops suggesting Local `#file:` and `#tool:` references for Copilot targets.
- Marks authored Local references unused with harness-specific guidance.
- Gives tool-set references a specific diagnostic explaining that Copilot requires individual tools in frontmatter.
- Preserves Local, prompt, instruction, skill, and Claude body behavior.

This PR is stacked on #342887 and is part of #342854.

## Testing

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- Targeted ESLint for changed body-language providers and tests — passed
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/languageProviders/promptBodyAutocompletion.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/languageProviders/promptHovers.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/languageProviders/promptValidator.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptSyntax/languageProviders/promptDocumentSemanticTokensProvider.test.ts` — passed, 220 tests

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call, version-keyed cache miss after edits, full-content parser implementation, all-prompt registration, and trigger-character `onDidType` call path are directly traced. Exact latency varies with document size and whether another feature happened to populate the same-version cache first, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread CPU plus full-document string, line-array, and YAML parse allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On each cache-cold model version, cost grows linearly with the complete prompt document; typing any registered trigger character (`.`, `:`, `/`, `\`, or `{`) can repeat that work even when the cursor is not in a reference.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased input-to-suggestion latency and transient allocation/GC pressure while editing larger prompt, instruction, skill, or agent documents.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The provider first inspected frontmatter delimiters and the current line in `findVariableReference`; irrelevant trigger characters returned without copying, splitting, or parsing the complete model.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every completion invocation now synchronously calls `getParsedPromptFile` and resolves the target before checking whether the current line contains a relevant `#...` or `{{...` reference.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 55 unconditionally invokes `this.promptsService.getParsedPromptFile(model)` ahead of the pre-existing line-local `findVariableReference` check; no equivalent full-model parse existed on this completion path before the PR.
Findings.Title: Keep irrelevant completion triggers on the line-local fast path
Findings.Impact: With trigger-character suggestions enabled, ordinary prose such as periods and paths invokes this provider immediately after an edit. The edit advances the model version, so `PromptsService.getParsedPromptFile` misses its version cache and calls `model.getValue()`, splits the whole document, and, for agents, parses the YAML header before suggestions can proceed. Large customization documents can therefore make common keystrokes and suggestion display noticeably slower.
Findings.Evidence: `PromptBodyAutocompletion` is registered for all prompt language selectors and declares common trigger characters including `.` and `/`. The changed line calls `getParsedPromptFile` before `findVariableReference`. `PromptsService.getParsedPromptFile` caches by model version but on a miss executes `new PromptFileParser().parse(textModel.uri, textModel.getValue())`; parser construction splits the full content, and `getTarget` reads `header.target`, forcing YAML parsing for agent files. VS Code's suggest model invokes providers directly from `onDidType` for their trigger characters. Thus a fresh edit realistically puts whole-document synchronous work on the input/suggestion critical path even when no completion can be returned.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the current-line fast path: first reject invocations that are neither inside a `#` reference nor an open `{{` placeholder, and only then resolve the parsed target. This keeps Copilot suppression and placeholder completion behavior while avoiding whole-document parsing for unrelated trigger characters.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing and invoking body completions in prompt, instruction, skill, and agent editors
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The suggest model invokes this provider from the editor's `onDidType` trigger-character listener. The newly added target lookup synchronously parses a cache-cold model before the provider can reject an irrelevant cursor position, so that parse is on the input-to-suggestion critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a directory to enumerate `#file:` completion candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one directory resolution per applicable non-Copilot file-reference completion invocation; child suggestions are served by that grouped resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one-resolution file-completion path existed before the diff. The regression is the newly preceding synchronous whole-document parse, not added filesystem fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before file suggestions are returned, but not reached for irrelevant trigger characters and no longer reached for GitHub Copilot agents because they return from the placeholder branch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Complete document byte and line count per edited model version. Common trigger characters such as `.` and `/` can invoke the work repeatedly; the effective parse cardinality is one per version unless another feature has already populated the same-version cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider execution begins synchronously on the editor thread. The prompts-service cache coalesces only repeated reads of the same model version; each edit creates a new version and therefore a new potential parse.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm reads at an unchanged version reuse the cached AST. A trigger character is itself an edit, so the normal immediate invocation is cache-cold unless semantic tokens or another provider has already parsed that exact version. There is no negative-cache issue.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registration, editor trigger dispatch, changed call order, version-keyed cache, full-model copy/split, and agent YAML parsing are directly established in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most customization files are small, and an independently populated same-version cache can mask the cost. Large instruction/skill documents and ordinary punctuation make the scaling mechanism realistic, but exact milliseconds are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity synchronous UI regression: the diff moves O(document-size) parse and allocation work ahead of the former line-local rejection path for all prompt languages.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live validation of GitHub Copilot agent body placeholders and Local references
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Validation is deferred and coalesced for 200 ms after edits. Parsing and marker creation must complete before diagnostics update, but this work is off the immediate keystroke path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existence check per effective filesystem-backed markdown link; before the diff GitHub Copilot Local `#file:` references also generated one check each.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All resolvable Local and markdown file references could schedule existence checks. The diff suppresses checks for Copilot Local `#file:` references while preserving markdown-link checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Checks are awaited before diagnostics publish, but the new early `continue` removes this boundary for Copilot Local references rather than adding it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the user home location for tilde references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per validation due to `userHome ??=`, and now skipped for Copilot Local references rejected by the changed branch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same lazy grouped lookup existed; the changed branch can only reduce its reachability for Copilot Local references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited only when a remaining tilde reference requires it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Body line count plus effective counts of placeholders, file references, and tool references in the open agent document.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One `Delayer` per visible model coalesces rapid edits. Existing file-reference checks are collected and awaited together; tool and placeholder checks are synchronous in-memory loops.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The parsed AST is cached by model version and its body arrays are lazily parsed once per AST. Validation generally consumes the latest coalesced version. No additional long-lived cache or retained-key state is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: validation scheduling, body parsing, loops, and filesystem call cardinality are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent bodies and reference counts vary, but placeholder/tool processing is simple in-memory work and validation is debounced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding. The added regex and marker loops are linear and coalesced; the only changed expensive-boundary behavior reduces filesystem work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Semantic highlighting and hover for GitHub Copilot placeholders
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Semantic tokens synchronously parse the current AST/body and encode all placeholder ranges before highlighting returns. Hover parses/reuses the AST and scans reference arrays until the hovered range is found.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Document body size for lazy parsing and number of placeholder/tool/file references for token mapping, sorting, and hover scans.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each provider call is synchronous until completion; cancellation is checked while encoding semantic tokens. There is no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work on these changed paths.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt ASTs are cached by model version and each `PromptBody` memoizes its parsed arrays. Warm hover/token calls reuse body parsing; edits invalidate at the version level. No unbounded cache or negative-cache behavior is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the parser, map/sort/token encoding, and hover loops are directly traced with no hidden boundary calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extremely large bodies or unusually many placeholders increase linear CPU/allocation work, but normal documents have low reference cardinality and this work directly implements the requested editor feature.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added work is bounded, linear in the document/reference count, memoized per AST version, and necessary for the newly supported highlighting and hover behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all ten changed files and their relevant callers. Submitted one finding for unconditional whole-document parsing on common completion triggers; no cache-lifecycle, concurrency-burst, cleanup, retained-memory, or newly introduced boundary-fanout regression was established elsewhere.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
